quickSummary: The mole is the SI base unit containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ entities. At IUPAC STP (0°C, 1 bar), 1 mole of ideal gas occupies 22.71 L. Vapor density relative to H₂ provides the golden relation M ≈ 2 × VD.
summary: Understand the three interconversion pathways of the mole, IUPAC STP standards, and gas density mechanics.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3. The Mole Concept & Conversion Triad
conceptBreakdown.title: 3. The Mole Concept & Conversion Triad

summaryBox.title: The Mole Triad Formulae
summaryBox.takeaway: n = w / M (Mass) = N / N_A (Count) = V_STP / V_m (Gas Volume).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE MOLE CONVERSION TRIAD
                                        │
         ┌──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                              ▼                              ▼
  MASS INTERCONVERSION          PARTICLE COUNT                 GAS MOLAR VOLUME
  $$n = \frac{w}{M}$$           $$n = \frac{N}{N_A}$$          $$n = \frac{V_{\text{STP}}}{V_m}$$
  ($w = \text{mass in g}$)      ($N = \text{count}$)           ($V_m = 22.71\text{ L at IUPAC STP}$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Since the 2019 SI redefinition, 1 mole contains exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (N_A).

• **Mass Path**: $n = \frac{w}{M}$ where $w$ is mass in grams and $M$ is molar mass in g/mol.
• **Particle Count Path**: $n = \frac{N}{N_A}$ where $N$ is count of atoms, molecules, or ions.
• **Gas Volume Path**: $n = \frac{V_{\text{STP}}}{V_m}$ where $V_m$ is molar volume at STP.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) Definitions
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) Definitions
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **IUPAC Current STP (Since 1982)**: $T = 273.15\text{ K } (0^\circ\text{C})$, $P = 1.0\text{ bar } (10^5\text{ Pa})$.
  $$\mathbf{V_m = 22.7109\text{ L/mol} = 22.71\text{ dm}^3\text{/mol}}$$

• **Old Classical STP (Pre-1982)**: $T = 273.15\text{ K } (0^\circ\text{C})$, $P = 1.0\text{ atm } (101.325\text{ kPa})$.
  $$\mathbf{V_m = 22.414\text{ L/mol} = 22.4\text{ dm}^3\text{/mol}}$$

• **SATP (Standard Ambient T & P)**: $T = 298.15\text{ K } (25^\circ\text{C})$, $P = 1.0\text{ bar}$.
  $$\mathbf{V_m = 24.789\text{ L/mol}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Vapor Density (VD) Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Vapor Density (VD) Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.content:
Vapor Density is the density of a gas relative to Hydrogen gas under identical T and P:

$$\text{VD} = \frac{d_{\text{gas}}}{d_{\text{H}_2}} = \frac{M_{\text{gas}}}{2.016} \implies \mathbf{Molar Mass (M) \approx 2 \times Vapor Density (VD)}$$

• **Average Molar Mass of Gas Mixtures (M̄)**:
$$\mathbf{\bar{M} = \frac{\sum (n_i M_i)}{\sum n_i} = \frac{\sum (V_i M_i)}{\sum V_i} = \sum (x_i M_i)}$$

quickRevision: Current IUPAC STP (1 bar) molar volume = 22.71 L/mol.
Legacy STP (1 atm) molar volume = 22.414 L/mol.
